methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $23M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 5 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

private.name: Humanoid
private.rationale: Same sector (Robotics & Manufacturing), same stage (Series A), post-money $1.35B

data.narrative:
Podium Automation is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $23M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private robotics firms at seed through Series B stages, plus one public comparable, providing multiple triangulation anchors within the sector.

Two methods apply here. Stage-progression modeling, using total raised as a proxy baseline, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-later-stage progression, yielding $46M. Peer-median valuation anchors on five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies—Generalist AI ($2.0B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B), Dexterity ($1.6B), Humanoid ($1.4B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B)—producing a median of $1.6B with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B. The wide dispersion reflects stage heterogeneity: three peers at Series B versus one at Series A and one at seed within the sample.

The triangulated range is $39M (floor) to $1.9B (ceiling), with a median of $848M. This wide band reflects material tension between stage-progression (which weights early funding velocity) and peer-median (which reflects later-stage and potentially well-capitalized comparable outcomes). Key uncertainties include the appropriate stage adjustment for Podium within the peer set, technology differentiation relative to Humanoid and Bedrock, and whether later-stage peer valuations represent sustainable market pricing or momentum-driven outliers.
